claim: Every cryocooler has a load curve/capacity map relating the maximum heat load it can remove to its operating temperature; loads above the nominal operating point drive the stage to a higher temperature, and the base temperature is set by the balance between cooling capacity and parasitic load.

location: Section 2.1 '50 K and 4 K Refrigeration', p. 3-4 (arXiv v1)

claim: Heat loads above (below) a cryocooler's operating point give higher (lower) stage temperatures; the base temperature is a balance of cooling capacity and parasitic loading (steady-state heat balance).
